title: Abraham, Sarah and a Promise
bigQuestion: What does the story say a promise can do for a family?

story.title: More Stars Than You Can Count
story.kicker: One night, an old man walks out of his tent and looks up.
paragraphs: It is night in the desert. A man named Abraham steps out of his tent. The air is cool. The sky is black and full of stars. He tips his head back and looks up.
Genesis tells this story. Abraham and his wife Sarah are old. They have no children. That makes them sad. The story says God tells Abraham to look at the sky.
Try to count the stars, the story says God tells him. Abraham looks. He counts one, two, three. Then ten. Then a hundred. There are too many to count.
The story says God makes a promise. Abraham's family will be as many as the stars. Abraham looks up one more time. Then he goes back into the tent to tell Sarah.
story.think: Have you ever tried to count the stars? What did it feel like?

lessons.title: Abraham and Sarah Set Out
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Abraham and Sarah left home because God told them to go.
reading: Genesis is the first book of the Bible. It tells about a man named Abraham. He lived in a city called Ur. Later his family moved to a place called Haran.
The story says God spoke to Abraham. God said, go to a new land. I will show you where. Abraham was not young. He was seventy-five years old.
Abraham packed up his tents. His wife Sarah came too. So did his nephew Lot. They walked a long way. The story calls the new land *Canaan*.

words.d: the first book of the Bible; it tells the story of Abraham's family
the name the story gives to the land Abraham and Sarah walked to

look.title: Picture It
look.text: Look at a tent folded up on a camel's back. A bag of flour hangs beside it. An old man holds a walking stick. An old woman ties on her sandals. They do not know where they are going yet.
look.prompt: What would you pack if you had to walk to a new home?

check.q: Which book of the Bible tells about Abraham?
check.why: Genesis is the first book. It tells the story of Abraham and his family.

check.q: Why did Abraham leave home, in the story?
choices: The story says God told him to go
check.why: The story says God spoke to Abraham and told him to go to a new land.

check.q: Who went with Abraham?
choices: His wife Sarah and his nephew Lot
check.why: Genesis says Sarah and Lot went with Abraham on the trip.

lessons.title: A Promise Under the Stars
lessons.mainIdea: The story says God promised Abraham a family as many as the stars.
reading: A *promise* is when you say you will do something. Then you do it. The story says God made a big promise to Abraham.
God told Abraham to look at the night sky. Count the stars, if you can. Nobody can count them all. The story says, your family will be that many.
Abraham had no children yet. Still, the story says he believed the promise. This promise is very important to Jews, Christians and Muslims.

words.d: saying you will do something, and then doing it

look.title: Look Up and Count
look.text: The story says God took Abraham outside at night. God said, look at the sky. Count the stars if you can. Your family will be that many.
look.cite: Genesis 15, told in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Why do you think the story picks stars, and not rocks or trees?

check.q: What is a promise?
choices: Saying you will do something, and doing it
check.why: A promise means you say you will do something and then you do it.

check.q: What did the story say Abraham's family would be like?
check.why: Genesis says God told Abraham his family would be as many as the stars.

check.q: How many children did Abraham have when he got the promise?
check.why: Abraham and Sarah had no children yet when the story says God made the promise.

lessons.title: Isaac Is Born
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Sarah had a baby, Isaac, when she and Abraham were very old.
reading: Abraham and Sarah waited a long time. The story says three visitors came to their tent. One said Sarah would have a son. Sarah laughed. She was too old, she thought.
But the story says a baby was born. They named him *Isaac*. That name sounds like the word for laughing in Hebrew. Sarah said, now everyone will laugh with me.
Abraham also had a son named Ishmael with a woman named Hagar. Muslims tell stories about Abraham, Hagar and Ishmael too. Jews and Christians tell about Isaac most.

words.d: the son of Abraham and Sarah; his name sounds like laughing
the language most of the Old Testament was first written in

look.title: Why Laugh?
look.text: Sarah hears a voice say she will have a baby. She is very old. Her hair is white. She laughs to herself behind the tent door. Later, she holds a baby boy and laughs again. It is a different laugh.
look.prompt: How is the first laugh different from the second laugh?

check.q: What was the name of Abraham and Sarah's son?
check.why: Genesis says Abraham and Sarah named their son Isaac.

check.q: What does the name Isaac sound like in Hebrew?
check.why: The name Isaac sounds like the Hebrew word for laughing. Sarah laughed.

check.q: Who tells stories about Abraham?
check.why: All three traditions tell stories about Abraham. Muslims also tell of Hagar and Ishmael.

lessons.title: Rebekah at the Well
lessons.mainIdea: The story says a kind girl named Rebekah became Isaac's wife.
reading: Isaac grew up. Abraham wanted a wife for him. The story says he sent a helper back to Haran. The helper stopped by a *well* with his camels.
A girl came to get water. Her name was Rebekah. The helper asked for a drink. She gave him one. Then she gave water to all ten camels. That is a lot of water!
The helper knew she was kind. The story says Rebekah agreed to go. She married Isaac. Later they had twin boys.

words.d: a deep hole in the ground where people get water

look.title: Water for the Camels
look.prompt: Ten camels drink a lot. What does that tell you about Rebekah?

check.q: Where did the helper meet Rebekah?
check.why: Genesis says the helper waited by a well, and Rebekah came to get water.

check.q: What did Rebekah do for the camels?
check.why: The story says Rebekah gave water to all the camels. It showed she was kind.

check.q: Who did Rebekah marry?
check.why: Rebekah married Isaac, the son of Abraham and Sarah.

lessons.title: Jacob and Esau
lessons.mainIdea: The story says twins Jacob and Esau fought, and then made up.
reading: Isaac and Rebekah had *twins*. Esau came out first. He was hairy and loved to hunt. Jacob came second. He liked to stay by the tents.
The twins did not get along. The story says Jacob tricked Esau two times. He got what was meant for the older brother. Esau was very angry. Jacob ran away.
Many years went by. The story says Jacob came home with gifts. Esau ran to meet him. He hugged him. They both cried. The brothers made up.

words.d: two children born to the same mother on the same day
Jacob's twin brother; he was born first and loved to hunt

look.title: The Brothers Meet Again
look.text: The story says Jacob was afraid to see Esau. He bowed down seven times. But Esau ran to him. Esau hugged him and kissed him. They both cried.
look.cite: Genesis 33, told in simple words from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Jacob was scared. What did Esau do instead of being mean?

check.q: Who were the twins?
check.why: Genesis says Isaac and Rebekah's twin sons were Esau and Jacob.

check.q: Which twin was born first?
check.why: The story says Esau was born first. Jacob came second.

check.q: How does the story of the twins end?
check.why: Genesis 33 says Esau ran to Jacob, hugged him, and they made up.

lessons.title: A Ladder to the Sky
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Jacob dreamed of a ladder with angels going up and down.
reading: Jacob was running away from Esau. Night came. He had no bed. He put a stone under his head and went to sleep.
The story says he had a *dream*. He saw a ladder. The bottom was on the ground. The top reached the sky. Angels went up and down on it.
In the dream, the story says God spoke. God gave Jacob the same promise as Abraham. Jacob woke up. He named the place Bethel.

words.d: pictures and stories you see while you sleep
in the Bible, a messenger sent from God

look.title: See the Ladder
look.text: Look at a boy asleep on the ground. A rock is his pillow. Above him a ladder goes up and up, into the stars. Angels step up the ladder. Other angels step down. Nobody is in a hurry.
look.prompt: Why do you think the angels go both up and down?

check.q: What did Jacob use for a pillow?
check.why: Genesis says Jacob put a stone under his head to sleep.

check.q: What did Jacob see in his dream?
check.why: The story says Jacob dreamed of a ladder to the sky with angels on it.

check.q: What did God tell Jacob in the dream, in the story?
choices: The same promise given to Abraham
check.why: Genesis 28 says God repeated the promise made to Abraham.

lessons.title: A Family Tree
lessons.mainIdea: The story says Jacob had twelve sons, and you can draw the whole family as a tree.
reading: Jacob got married. The story says he had two wives, Leah and Rachel. Jacob had twelve sons and a daughter named Dinah. That is a big family!
A *family tree* is a drawing. It shows who is whose parent. Abraham and Sarah go at the top. Isaac is under them. Jacob is under Isaac.
The story says God gave Jacob a new name. The name was Israel. The twelve sons became twelve big families. Jews call them the twelve tribes of Israel.

words.d: a drawing that shows parents, children and grandchildren
the new name the story says God gave to Jacob

look.title: Count the Family
look.prompt: Which row has the biggest number? Whose family is that?

check.q: How many sons did Jacob have?
check.why: Genesis says Jacob had twelve sons. They became the twelve tribes.

check.q: What is a family tree?
choices: A drawing of parents and children
check.why: A family tree is a drawing that shows who is whose parent and child.

check.q: What new name did the story say God gave Jacob?
check.why: Genesis 35 says God named Jacob Israel.

review.why: Sarah was Abraham's wife. Rebekah married Isaac, and Rachel married Jacob.

review.q: What did the story say God told Abraham to count?
review.why: Genesis 15 says God told Abraham to count the stars, if he could.
The name Isaac sounds like the Hebrew word for laughing.

review.q: Who gave water to ten camels?
review.why: Genesis 24 says Rebekah gave water to the helper and his camels.

review.q: Where was the top of the ladder in Jacob's dream?
review.why: The story says the ladder stood on the ground and reached the sky.

review.q: Which is the right order, oldest to youngest?
review.why: Abraham was Isaac's father. Isaac was Jacob's father.
